clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms. The operative sentence exempts Maurice C. Latta from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year and fixes the last day: "one year ending October 31, 1942". The end is recorded as 1942-10-31, inclusive (the exemption runs through that day, per the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on stated end dates); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption ends when that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. The recital explains why the exemption is wanted and adds no separate command. The earlier exemption orders recited in the text are earlier instruments and do not bear on this order's end. The packet's searches (number citations, Federal Register catalog notes, person-name search) show no later order that changes the period or ends the exemption earlier; see the order-level checks. EO 9238 of September 3, 1942, which recites this order's period, further exempts the same employee; it is recorded as a later event and is not an end of this order (it neither amends the stated period nor revokes the order).

research_rationale:
Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8904-exemption-maurice-c-latta-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-11-04: the APP mirror page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl (Common Crawl capture 2025-10-07T00:24:47Z) has the heading "Executive Order 8904—Exemption of Maurice C. Latta From Compulsory Retirement for Age", its date (1941-09-22) and subject agree with the held text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. Identity: the register lists this number with date 1941-09-22, signer Franklin D. Roosevelt and the title "Exemption of Maurice C. Latta From Compulsory Retirement for Age"; the held text concerns Maurice C. Latta and ends with the signature "FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT" and the date line "September 22, 1941.". Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy.
Content: the order has one recital and one operative sentence. It exempts one named employee, Maurice C. Latta (Executive Clerk, The White House Office, Executive Office of the President), from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), for a period of one year ending October 31, 1942. The recital says he "was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 8256 of September 20, 1939, and No. 8497 of July 26, 1940" and asks that he "be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year"; the earlier exemption orders it recites are earlier instruments, not later events, and not ends of this order. The inventory is therefore one clause, the exemption. Extension reading: this order is the further exemption; any later exemption of the same person would be a new exercise of the section 204 power with its own period and a later event, not an end of this order, and EO 9238 is such an order (below).
Later event: EO 9238 of September 3, 1942 (APP node 371719; page check done 2026-11-04 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl: heading "Executive Order 9238—Exemption of Rudolph Forster and Maurice C. Latta from Compulsory Retirement for Age", date 1942-09-03, text_sha256 equal to the held file's, Common Crawl capture 2025-06-12T16:58:17Z) exempts Rudolph Forster and further exempts Maurice C. Latta, Executive Clerk, The White House Office. Its recital says Latta "who has heretofore been exempted from compulsory retirement for age until October 31, 1942", which is the same position and the same last day as this order; its operative sentence ("are hereby exempted and further exempted, respectively, from compulsory retirement for age" "the said Rudolph Forster and Maurice C. Latte", which spells his surname "Latte") states no period. It does not revoke, supersede or amend this order and it recites this order's exemption as a completed grant, so it is a further exemption recorded as a later event with its own date and quote (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on further exemptions), not this order's end. The period it grants after October 31, 1942 is not this order's command.
